questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The language spoken in the country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I wasn't aware there was an email for the university where we were given many of the arrival informations, and therefore wasn't sure, where and how the check in rutine was.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I asked students, where the different buildings for the check in were.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It was nice living on campus, and thereby having the easy opportunity to go home between the modules.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The cooking facilities were good, but wasn't aware of all the cutlery, pots and pans we needed to by ourself.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The need to by cooking supplies, beddings and pillow/ duvet yourself.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I expected to have some social relationship to the people I lived next to, but there wasn't any social gatherings with the people I lived at the some corridor with

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The course registration process was very difficult, as many of the courses required prerequisites before being able to register the course. You therefore had to research every course for prerequisites, and your courses from home weren't taken to account as prerequisite. In addition not all of the courses were available for the term you were abroad, and also had to take that in mind.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: the registration process was very long, and at times hard to manage. there were many dates to remember and processes to do.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a sps mentor to guide me through the process

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: many of the courses have different structures and prerequisites, and therefore it's a good idea to know what type of course it is, and if it's available the term you are abroad.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses academic level seemed lower than Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: 3 out of 4 courses was with 100+ student lectures, with no group work, and therefore didn't get to know any of your classmates. The wasn't and required readings before the class for some of the courses, were the only literature was the powerpoints. Also the tests and exams were multiple choice, which was a new way of being tested.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Psychology of human movement science, psychology of exercise, exercise nutrition, introduction to kinesiology management

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I found the management course extra interesting, as it wasn't a cause that wasn't offered in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I joined the badminton club at the university, which I was really glad I did. I learned many people from club, and ended up being many best friends during the stay

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join some clubs, as it's a really good way to learn some local people, and get to know some people.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: London itself doesn't have many things to offer, therefore going to Toronto, Niagara or the USA, is an easy thing to do during the holiday or weekend.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The culture in Canada is very similar to Denmark and Europe, therefore didn't any major adjustments needed.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: join some clubs

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The students are generally younger than in Denmark, were in some points could feel they maybe were a bit more immature.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They were very opened to ask how you're day has been

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Remember to explore the country you are going to visit, as you might not come to the country again.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: As the school doesn't hold any exchange get togethers, make an effort to join clubs, ore meet with other exchange students from your country, to know some people while you're studying

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: getting to learn some other things, I wasn't able to learn if studying in Denmark and getting to learn new people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to adapt to the new exam format

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
